stem: Pemberton Labs' new hire asks why a `resource "aws_instance"` block works when Terraform's core program has never heard of an EC2 instance. Which answer is correct?

choices.text: Terraform core ships with a small built-in library of the most common cloud resource types, including EC2 instances.
The `aws` provider itself defines the `aws_instance` resource type; Terraform core just calls whichever provider owns a resource type's implementation.
The Terraform Registry rewrites the configuration file at `init` time to replace `aws_instance` with the provider's own private syntax.
The block that names the provider and its version constraint itself contains the full definition of every resource type that provider can create, including all of its individual arguments.

rationale: The provider itself adds the resource types it supports, so `aws_instance` exists because the `aws` provider defines it, not because Terraform core knows about EC2. Terraform core has no built-in catalog of cloud resource types; that contradicts the plugin model entirely. The registry distributes provider plugins; it does not rewrite a user's configuration file at `init` time. `required_providers` only names a provider and a version constraint, not a catalog of that provider's resource-type definitions.
